project.objective: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?

questions.question: Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?
questions.rationale: Reuben Spencer Spriggs has no parent links in the tree. The 1900 US census should show him as an infant in his parents' household, likely still in Benson County, North Dakota, making it the highest-priority record for identifying both parents by name. North Dakota birth registers and the 1910 census (which places him in Beadle County, South Dakota) offer corroborating avenues. His WWI draft card and obituary may also name a parent or birthplace detail that narrows the search.

search_stop.justification: Overturn risk: low. Three independent sources from two separate creation periods (1898 and 1910) consistently name John W Spriggs and Charlotte (née Westby) Spriggs as Reuben Spencer Spriggs's parents: (1) the ELCA baptism record of 6 November 1898 naming J W Spriggs and Charlotte Spriggs as parents at the event; (2) the 1910 US federal census in Beadle County, SD, with Reuben listed as son in their household; and (3) the 19 August 1898 Spokane, Washington marriage record of John W Spriggs and Charlotte Westby, 11 weeks before Reuben's birth. FamilySearch 1900 census exhaustively searched across 10+ name variants — negative (likely misindexed infant). No civil birth certificate exists for a November 1898 Benson County birth (ND statewide registration began 1907). Remaining unsearched sources are paywalled (Ancestry 1900 census) or privacy-sealed (California 1998 death certificate), and neither is likely to name different parents given three converging sources.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. Three independent sources directly name John W Spriggs and Charlotte (née Westby) Spriggs as Reuben's parents: the 1898 ELCA baptism (parents named at the event), the 1910 US census (Reuben listed as son in their household), and the 1898 Spokane marriage record (John W Spriggs married Charlotte Westby 11 weeks before Reuben's birth).
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. Searched: 1900 federal census (FamilySearch, 10+ name variants, exhaustive, negative); 1910 federal census (positive); 1915 ND state census (positive, different Spriggs family); ELCA church baptism records 1894–1903 (positive); ND County Marriages 1872–2000 (negative — marriage occurred in Washington state, found via US-wide search); ND Red River Valley Pioneer Files (negative); ND Cemetery Records (FAN-cluster, positive for related Spriggs). FAN-cluster research attempted. No civil birth certificate exists for a 1898 Benson County birth (registration began 1907). The baptism is the correct primary substitute and was found.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. All three key sources accessed as original records via direct record_read: ELCA baptism (log_009, image ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C9PT-V9Q2-2 cited); 1910 census (original federal enumeration); Spokane marriage record (log_029, image ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GTM4-GR9 cited). Index results used only to locate records; confirmed by direct reads.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Three sources with distinct informants and institutional origins: (1) ELCA church register, 1898 — parents as primary informants at the baptism; (2) 1910 US federal census — government enumerator visiting the household; (3) 1898 Washington State civil marriage record — civil official recording the marriage license. No two share the same informant or creation process.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The 1898 ELCA baptism is an original church register with primary information about Reuben's parentage — parents present and named contemporaneously. ND statewide birth registration began 1907 (confirmed: North Dakota Vital Records wiki); no civil birth certificate exists for 1898, making the baptism the designated substitute. The 1910 census is an original record with primary information about the census event.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. Minor discrepancies within normal bounds: 1-year census age rounding (implied birth 1899 vs actual 1898); baptism indexer transposition (stated birth 24 Nov vs christening 6 Nov — impossible sequence, christening date matches tree exactly). The 1915 ND Fred E Spriggs household is a separate family line, not a competing parentage. The Grace Spriggs ELCA marriage naming 'Imogine Spriggs' is a different Spriggs family. No unregistered disagreements (count 0), no open conflicts.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. No plausible unsearched record type could name different parents given three converging independent sources from two creation periods. Ancestry 1900 census (paywalled; FamilySearch version exhaustively searched, negative — likely misindexed infant) and California 1998 death certificate (privacy-sealed, heir-request only) remain beyond reach. Even if the 1900 census were found, it could only corroborate. No evidence points to alternative parents.

The June 1900 federal census would enumerate him as a ~1-year-old infant in his parents' household, directly naming the head of household and spouse. 'United States, Census, 1900' (collection 1325221) is name-searchable. This is the highest-probability record for identifying the parents. loc_001 (Benson County, 1890–1920) notes the 1890 federal census did not survive, making 1900 the first available federal census for this family. Try variant spellings: Sprigg, Springs.

items.rationale: The tree records Reuben's 1910 residence as Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota. At age 11 he would almost certainly still be living in his parents' household, so the 1910 census would name the parents directly. 'United States, Census, 1910' (collection 1727033) is name-searchable. If the 1900 Benson County census (item 2) fails to locate the household — due to misindexing or schedule damage — this Beadle County, South Dakota record provides an independent path to the parents and confirms the family's migration route. Try variant spellings: Sprigg, Springs.

Even if Reuben moved to South Dakota by 1910, his parents may have remained in Benson County through 1915. 'North Dakota, Census, 1915' (collection 2346284) is name-searchable. Finding a Spriggs household in Benson County in 1915 names the parents and may reveal siblings who stayed behind. Note: no 1905 North Dakota state census was held — the statewide state censuses are 1885 (territorial), 1915, and 1925.

A church baptism record is the primary substitute for a civil birth certificate under the poor early compliance flagged by loc_001: county-level civil registration started only 'late 1890s' with uneven compliance; statewide registration began in 1907. A baptism entry would directly name both parents and often the godparents. 'United States, Evangelical Lutheran Church in America records, ca. 1800-1900' (collection 2363041) is name-searchable and covers through 1900, putting Reuben's November 1898 birth within range. loc_001 notes Norwegian Lutheran was dominant in Benson County; however, 'Spriggs' is an English surname and the family may have belonged to a different denomination (Methodist, Presbyterian, or other) — search the ELCA collection first, then any available Maddock or Benson County church records outside the ELCA collection.

items.rationale: Once candidate parent names are obtained from the census (items 2–4), search for their marriage in North Dakota. 'North Dakota, County Marriages, 1872-2000' (collection 2550852) is name-searchable. The parents' marriage record supplies the mother's maiden name (commonly omitted on census records), confirms the couple as a unit, and by its date relative to Reuben's November 1898 birth corroborates a parentage claim resting otherwise on indirect or derivative evidence. Even before specific parent names are known, a name search on 'Spriggs' across Benson County marriages 1880–1898 is feasible given the surname's rarity in North Dakota. loc_001 flags that pre-1925 Benson County marriage records were NOT transferred to the State Historical Society of North Dakota — if the FamilySearch index is incomplete, consult the Benson County Courthouse directly.

'North Dakota, Red River Valley Genealogical Society, Pioneer Files, 1880-1953' (collection 3155904) is name-searchable. These compiled biographical and family files for North Dakota pioneer families may index the Spriggs family, naming Reuben's parents and siblings. As a required FAN-cluster item for a parentage question, entries for neighbors, associates, or persons of a different surname who mention a Spriggs family connection may also supply leads — a household neighbor in Benson County who mentions the Spriggs family in their own biography could name the parents directly.

'North Dakota, Cemetery Records, 1877-1999' (collection 1451475) is name-searchable. Searching for Spriggs in Benson County cemeteries identifies other family members buried there — parents, siblings, relatives — whose burial dates and epitaphs may supply the parents' names and lifespans. This is a FAN-cluster item: a sibling's headstone naming both parents would directly answer the question, and a parent's own gravestone confirms identity and lifespan bounds. Also search Beadle County, South Dakota cemeteries (Maplewood Cemetery, Iroquois, Kingsbury County is confirmed by the tree for Reuben himself) for any Spriggs family plot.

Reuben died 21 May 1998 in Riverside, Riverside County, California (confirmed by tree fact). California death certificates carry dedicated fields for the decedent's father's name and mother's maiden name. The informant at Reuben's death (likely a child — the tree shows a son and a daughter who survived him) would have direct knowledge of the grandparents' identities. As a derivative source for parentage, the accuracy depends on the informant's knowledge, but it provides candidate names to test against North Dakota records. Request through the California Department of Public Health, Vital Records Office, or the Riverside County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Who Were the Parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs?

Reuben Spencer Spriggs was born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota. The preponderance of evidence from three independent sources drawn from two distinct time periods strongly indicates that his parents were John W. Spriggs (born Iowa, about 1872) and Charlotte Spriggs, née Westby (born Norway, about 1877).

### 1898 ELCA Baptism Record

The earliest and most direct evidence is a baptismal register entry cited as "United States, Evangelical Lutheran Church in America records, ca. 1800-1900," database with images, *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:QK1L-SKL7 : 31 July 2026), 06 Nov 1898; citing Carrington, South Dakota, United States, Baptism; from *Ancestry*. www.ancestry.com, Multiple archives, United States; FHL microfilm 100,881,426 (record ark:/61903/1:1:QVN2-ZC27, image ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C9PT-V9Q2-2). This original church register names Ruben Spencer Spriggs as the child with father J W Spriggs and mother Charlotte Spriggs. As an original church record with the parents as primary informants — present at the baptism and naming the child and themselves at the time of the event — this entry provides primary information about Reuben's parentage, contemporaneously recorded in 1898.

One apparent discrepancy requires explanation: the FamilySearch index states the birth date as 24 November 1898 and the christening as 6 November 1898. A christening before birth is biologically impossible; this is an indexer transposition of the two dates. The actual birth was 6 November 1898 — consistent with both the established tree date and the 1910 census age — and the christening took place eighteen days later on 24 November 1898, a normal postnatal interval.

### 1898 Spokane, Washington Marriage Record

"Washington, County Marriages, 1855-2008," *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QPMT-3HSD : Sat Mar 09 17:34:45 UTC 2024), Entry for John W Spriggs and Charlotte Westby, 19 August 1898 (image ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GTM4-GR9) records that John W. Spriggs married Charlotte Westby on 19 August 1898 in Spokane, Washington. Both parties were primary informants about the marriage event. Reuben Spencer Spriggs was born eleven weeks later, on 6 November 1898, in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota. This civil record establishes the marital union of John W. Spriggs and Charlotte Westby — who appears in both the 1898 baptism register and the 1910 census under her married name Charlotte Spriggs — immediately preceding Reuben's birth.

### 1910 United States Federal Census

"United States, Census, 1910," *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9JX9-6LD : Wed Aug 13 17:11:01 UTC 2025), Entry for John W Spriggs and Charlotte Spriggs, 1910 (record ark:/61903/1:1:MPXD-MZC) enumerates Rueben S Spriggs (age 11, born North Dakota) as son in the household of John W. Spriggs (head, age 38, born Iowa) and Charlotte Spriggs (wife, age 33, born Norway) in Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota. The informant is unknown — the census does not record who answered the enumerator's questions — so the parentage information from this record is indeterminate in quality. Nevertheless, a government enumerator personally visited the dwelling and recorded the household composition during the 1910 enumeration. The record corroborates the 1898 baptism twelve years later and from a different institutional context. The implied birth year (about 1899 from age 11) differs from the actual birth of 6 November 1898 by one year, within normal census age-rounding variation.

### Additional Records Consulted

Two additional ELCA church records from the same register were examined as part of FAN-cluster research: the 30 November 1910 marriage of Fredrick Leigh and Grace Spriggs (ark:/61903/1:1:QVN2-ZDYK), which names the bride's father as John Spriggs and mother as Imogine Spriggs; and the 2 June 1931 marriage of Mils J and Myrtle E Brandvold (ark:/61903/1:1:QVN2-8WBF), which names the bride's father as Spriggs. Neither record pertains to John W. Spriggs or Charlotte Westby Spriggs; both are separate Spriggs family lines found in the same congregation's records. A 1915 North Dakota state census entry for Fred E. Spriggs (ark:/61903/1:1:QK94-K514) in Benson County also pertains to a different Spriggs household, not to Reuben's parents.

### Record Availability and Search Scope

No civil birth certificate exists for a child born in Benson County, North Dakota in November 1898: statewide birth registration in North Dakota did not begin until 1907. The 1898 ELCA baptism record is the appropriate primary substitute for a birth certificate and was accessed as an original church register image. The 1900 federal census was searched exhaustively on FamilySearch (collection 1325221) across ten or more name variants, returning no result for Reuben or his family; the infant was likely misindexed. No competing parentage candidates were identified in any source consulted.

### Conclusion

Three sources from two institutional origins — an 1898 church baptismal register (primary information), an 1898 civil marriage record (primary information establishing the couple), and a 1910 federal census (corroborating) — drawn from two creation periods consistently and independently identify John W. Spriggs and Charlotte (née Westby) Spriggs as the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs. No source names or implies any alternative parents. The preponderance of evidence strongly indicates that Reuben Spencer Spriggs is the son of John W. Spriggs and Charlotte Spriggs, née Westby.

# Locality Guide: Benson County, North Dakota (1890–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** March 9, 1883, from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties, Dakota Territory
- **County seat / administrative center:** Minnewaukan
- **Parent jurisdiction:** State of North Dakota (statehood November 2, 1889; records 1883–1889 filed under Dakota Territory)
- **Population during period:** 2,460 (1890); 8,320 (1900); 12,681 (1910); 13,095 (1920) — rapid growth driven by homesteading
- **Economy:** Dryland farming and grain agriculture; homestead-era settlement
- **Ethnic composition:** Large Norwegian immigrant community; German-Russian settlers; Spirit Lake Dakota (Sioux) community at Fort Totten
- **Religious denominations:** Lutheran (dominant among Norwegian settlers); other Protestant denominations; Catholic mission at Fort Totten
- **Key historical events:** Dakota Territory statehood (1889); mass homestead immigration 1890s–1910s; WWI draft (1917–1918)

## Boundary changes
- Benson County was created March 9, 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties, Dakota Territory. The FamilySearch Wiki states there is no known history of courthouse disasters in this county ([Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy)).
- The county became part of North Dakota at statehood on November 2, 1889. Records created 1883–1889 are Dakota Territory records.
- Boundaries were stable throughout the 1890–1920 research period.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** County-level birth records from the late 1890s (uneven compliance); county death records from 1895; county marriage records from the late 1800s — all held at the Benson County Courthouse, Clerk of District Court. Statewide registration of births and deaths began in 1907, with general compliance not reached until 1924. Statewide marriage registration began in 1925 ([North Dakota Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records)).
- **What exists:** County marriages 1872–2000 are indexed and imaged at FamilySearch (collection 2550852, 17,428 records). North Dakota death certificates 1908–2007 are at Ancestry (collection 61747, index & images, $). The North Dakota Department of Health Public Death Index (1892–present) is free online at apps.nd.gov. No online collection of Benson County birth certificates was returned by any tool in this survey.
- **Gaps:** Reuben Spriggs's November 1898 birth predates the statewide system and falls in the early, compliance-uncertain county period — a county birth entry may or may not exist. Church baptism records are the primary alternative.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Lutheran (Norwegian, predominant); other Protestant; Catholic mission at Fort Totten
- **Record types and digitization:** Two Benson County Lutheran volumes are digitized on FamilySearch: Flora Lutheran Church (imageGroupNumber 100881427, 1820–1997, English and Norwegian, 34% name-indexed — partly indexed + images) and Esmond Lutheran Church (imageGroupNumber 100881428, 1830–1958, English and Norwegian, 36% name-indexed — partly indexed + images). U.S. Evangelical Lutheran Church in America records 1875–1940 are also at Ancestry (collection 60722, index & images, $).
- **Language:** Norwegian appears alongside English in both digitized volumes. Older entries may require reading Norwegian script — a researcher must be prepared for this.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** The 1890 federal census for North Dakota did not survive ([Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy#Census_Records)). The 1900 census is the next available; FamilySearch has 1 Benson County volume (imageGroupNumber 004120517_002_M9LK-PZ1, 234 images, 92% name-indexed — **indexed + images**). The 1910 and 1920 federal censuses are indexed and available nationwide at FamilySearch and Ancestry but no Benson-specific volumes were separately returned in this survey.
- **State census:** North Dakota state censuses exist for 1885, 1915, and 1925. The 1885 Dakota Territory census is index-only (free) at NDSU Archives and index & images at Ancestry (collection 1078, $). The 1915 state census (FamilySearch collection 2346284, 619,486 records statewide) has two Benson County volumes: imageGroupNumber 007637091_003 (55% indexed) and 007637092 (51% indexed) — **partly indexed + images**. The 1925 state census is at FamilySearch (collection 2351024) and Ancestry.
- **Access:** 1900 federal and 1915 state censuses are free at FamilySearch; 1885 and 1925 state censuses are at Ancestry ($) and partly free.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories; court records from 1883 and probate from 1883 at county level
- **Where held:** Originals at Benson County Courthouse (Clerk District Court), Minnewaukan. Microfilm copies at the State Historical Society of North Dakota, Bismarck. Online: Ancestry has North Dakota and South Dakota Wills and Probate Records, 1800–1985 (collection 9081, index & images, $). FamilySearch full-text search also covers some probate.
- **Digitized court volumes:** Three court/miscellaneous volumes for Benson County are digitized on FamilySearch (imageGroupNumbers 007785642, 007786987), covering records from 1888 onward — **0% name-indexed, full-text searchable** (not browse-only; use full-text search at FamilySearch).

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Rectangular survey (public land survey system); most land entered via federal homestead or direct purchase from the GLO
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Federal General Land Office granted public domain land; after transfer, the Benson County Register of Deeds recorded deeds and mortgages from 1883. The Benson County Genealogy wiki page lists the BLM Land Records Index at USGenWeb Archives and BLM glorecords.blm.gov for federal patents ([Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy#Land_and_Property_Records)).
- **Online:** U.S. General Land Office Records 1796–1907 at Ancestry (collection 1246, index, free); U.S. Homestead Records 1863–1908 at Ancestry (collection 60593, index & images, $). Post-patent deeds at the county courthouse (physical only).

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** World War I (1917–1918) falls within the target period; Spanish-American War (1898) is background context
- **Record types:** WWI draft registration cards (nationwide, NARA, widely indexed online); North Dakota Military Men 1917–1918 at Ancestry (collection 4569, index only, $); WWI Roster of ND service members at Ancestry (collection 31404, images, $); Genealogy Trails has a Benson County WWI casualties list
- **Where held:** NARA holds draft registration cards (widely digitized); state copies at State Historical Society of North Dakota

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** North Dakota Cemetery Records 1877–1999 at FamilySearch (collection 1451475, 546,565 records, **indexed + images**); also FindAGrave, BillionGraves, USGenWeb Tombstone Project (usgwtombstones.org/northdakota/benson.html), and Interment.net
- **Physical records:** Sexton records held locally; FamilySearch Library holds tombstone transcription microfilm for the county
- **List of cemeteries:** FindAGrave (findagrave.com/cemetery-browse/USA/North-Dakota/Benson-County) and BillionGraves

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Maddock and Minnewaukan (county seat) had local papers during this period. Genealogy Trails has transcribed Benson County marriage announcements and obituaries (genealogytrails.com/ndak/benson/).
- **Where held:** Chronicling America (LOC, free) has some North Dakota newspapers; GenealogyBank ($, 1865–1931); NewspaperArchive ($, 1873–1994); State Historical Society of North Dakota maintains an inventory and catalog of all known ND newspapers. The NDSU Obituary Index (library.ndsu.edu/db/obituary/) is a free index.
- **Content value:** Obituaries commonly name parents and surviving relatives — critical for identifying Reuben's parents. Marriage announcements and legal notices also appear.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Benson County lies roughly 75 miles south of the Canadian border (Manitoba/Saskatchewan). Many settlers arrived via Canada; Canadian border crossing records are often more relevant than Atlantic port manifests.
- **Record types:** North Dakota Manifests of Immigrant Arrivals, 1910–1952 (FamilySearch collection 2443935, 19,294 records, indexed + images); US Border Crossings from Canada, 1894–1954 (FamilySearch collection 2185932, indexed + images); North Dakota and South Dakota Naturalization Records, 1851–1924 (FamilySearch collection 3241319, indexed + images); Pioneer Files 1880–1953 (FamilySearch collection 3155904, indexed).
- **Naturalization — exceptional local coverage:** Five digitized volumes of Benson County District Court declarations of intention and final papers/petitions, covering 1884–1955 (imageGroupNumbers 007785641–007785645), are available on FamilySearch — **0% name-indexed, full-text searchable**. Use FamilySearch full-text search. General index volumes (imageGroupNumber 007785645) are the entry point. Originals at the State Historical Society of North Dakota, Bismarck.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all members.

### Tax records
- **Types:** County property tax and personal property tax
- **Date range:** Available from county formation (1883)
- **Where held:** Benson County Courthouse (treasurer's, auditor's, or clerk's office); some records moved to the North Dakota State Archives, Bismarck ([Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy#Tax_Records))
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists can substitute for the lost 1890 federal census and fill gaps between census years

### Other record types
- **Fort Totten / Spirit Lake Reservation:** The Spirit Lake Reservation (also historically called Devils Lake Reservation) is located primarily in Benson County. Fort Totten Indian Agency records are digitized on FamilySearch (imageGroupNumbers 008271676 and 008273622): annual census 1881–1941, births 1924–1945, deaths 1881–1945, school records 1930–1942, and probate 1892–1936 — all **full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed**.
- **School records:** Maddock High School graduates 1917–1925 are transcribed at Genealogy Trails (genealogytrails.com/ndak/benson/schools_maddock.html). No other school record digitization was returned for this survey.
- **Local histories:** *The First Fifty Years: A History of the Community of Maddock, North Dakota, 1901–1951* (FamilySearch catalog koha:2205557) is available online at the FamilySearch Digital Library — directly relevant to Reuben's birthplace and may contain Spriggs family entries.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | 1900 census (92% indexed); 1915 state census (partly indexed); county marriages 1872–2000 (indexed + images); cemetery records 1877–1999 (indexed + images); naturalization records 1868–1924 (indexed + images); naturalization declarations/petitions 1884–1955 (full-text); Fort Totten agency records (full-text); Pioneer Files 1880–1953 | Free |
| Ancestry | Territorial/state censuses 1885/1915/1925; county marriages; death certificates 1908–2007; naturalization records 1873–1952; naturalization index 1874–1963; ELCA church records 1875–1940; wills/probate 1800–1985; homestead records | Subscription ($) |
| MyHeritage | Naturalizations 1870–1968; deaths 1893+; biography records; border crossings from Canada 1895–1956 | Subscription ($) |
| BLM GLO Records (glorecords.blm.gov) | Federal land patents and homestead entries | Free |
| Chronicling America (LOC) | North Dakota newspapers | Free |
| NDSU Archives (library.ndsu.edu) | 1885 census index; ND naturalization index; biography index; obituary index | Free |
| State Historical Society of ND (history.nd.gov) | Marriage database (selected counties; Benson County pre-1925 marriages not in transferred set); genealogy research guide | Free index / in-person |
| Genealogy Trails (genealogytrails.com/ndak/benson/) | Marriage announcements; obituaries; biographies; WWI casualties; school records | Free |
| USGenWeb Archives (usgwarchives.net/nd/benson/) | Land records index; cemetery transcriptions; miscellaneous records | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** The `volume_search` returned all 13 digitized volumes matching Benson County for the 1890–1920 period — this is the complete result set.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Benson County Courthouse, 311 B Ave St, Minnewaukan ND 58351 (701-473-5345) | Birth records (late 1890s+), marriage records (late 1800s+), death records (1895+), court/probate/divorce records (1883+), land records (1883+) | In-person or mail |
| State Historical Society of North Dakota, Bismarck | Naturalization records microfilm (originals); ND newspaper collection; county record microfilm | In-person; some ILL; online index |
| NARA — Kansas City | Federal naturalization records; WWI draft registration cards | In-person; most draft cards digitized online |
| FamilySearch Library, Salt Lake City | Microfilm of Benson County naturalization records; 1885 census index; local history books including Maddock history | In-person or via FamilySearch Center |

## Records NOT online
- Benson County birth certificates (held at Benson County Courthouse; FamilySearch Library has not acquired ND birth or death records from the state)
- Benson County death certificates before 1908 (county records from 1895 at courthouse; state Ancestry series begins 1908)
- Benson County tax records (at county treasurer's/auditor's office; some at ND State Archives)
- Benson County court minute books before digitized range (courthouse holds originals from 1883)
- Most local church records beyond the Flora and Esmond Lutheran volumes

## Known record losses
- The 1890 federal census for North Dakota did not survive — this is a statewide loss confirmed by the FamilySearch Wiki ([Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy#Census_Records)). The 1885 territorial census and 1900 federal census are the flanking substitutes.
- The FamilySearch Wiki states there is no known history of courthouse disasters in Benson County — records from 1883 should be physically intact at the courthouse.

## Research tips
- **The 1900 federal census is the single highest-priority record** for identifying Reuben's parents. It should show him as an infant in his parents' household in Benson County. The Benson County volume (92% name-indexed) is searchable at FamilySearch.
- **Birth records for 1898 are uncertain.** Statewide birth registration began in 1907; county-level records started in the "late 1890s" with uneven compliance. Request a search of the early birth register from the Benson County Courthouse (Clerk District Court, Minnewaukan), but do not assume one exists ([Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy#County_Courthouse); [North Dakota Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records)).
- **Church records are the primary birth substitute.** The county had a substantial Norwegian Lutheran population. The Flora and Esmond Lutheran Church volumes on FamilySearch are partly indexed; the ELCA database at Ancestry covers more. Identifying the family's denomination first makes the search tractable ([North Dakota Research Tips and Strategies](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Research_Tips_and_Strategies)).
- **Use the 1915 state census.** It fills the gap between the 1910 and 1920 federal censuses and is partly indexed at FamilySearch (collection 2346284) and fully at Ancestry.
- **Check naturalization records for immigrant parents.** The Benson County District Court naturalization volumes (declarations 1884–1954, petitions 1888–1955) are full-text searchable on FamilySearch; the general index (imageGroupNumber 007785645) is the entry point. These records name the applicant's birthplace and country of origin.
- **The Maddock local history is freely available online.** *The First Fifty Years: A History of Maddock, North Dakota, 1901–1951* (FamilySearch catalog koha:2205557) may contain a Spriggs family biography or history entry.
